articles.summary: SpaceX founder Elon Musk ordered restrictions on a military-grade satellite communications network used by Ukrainian forces, disrupting drone operations and triggering confusion within the Trump administration, according to a new report. Musk ordered a slowdown of Starshield, a military-grade version of the company’s Starlink satellite network that Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter. The restrictions reportedly rendered some Ukrainian attack drones and interceptor drones virtually useless, hampering the country’s ability to strike Russian forces and defend against aerial attacks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that decisions regarding Ukraine’s access to the network belonged to SpaceX and Musk, rather than the White House, and denied having advance knowledge of the move. “I’m not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. But that’s irrelevant,” Rubio told reporters during a visit to India. “The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how their stuff can be used and what speeds they’ll allow it to be used at.”

articles.author: Lynn La
articles.summary: A tablet at the counter of the Department of Motor Vehicles in Fresno on Oct. 2, 2026. Photo by Larry Valenzuela for CalMatters Perhaps today is not the best day to go to the DMV. California state workers are planning a one-day strike today in multiple cities including Sacramento, San Francisco and Los Angeles. They’re protesting what they say are unfair labor practices by Gov. Gavin Newsom’s administration. The work stoppage could affect services at the DMV, unemployment offices and other departments. SEIU Local 1000 represents about 100,000 workers employed in dozens of agencies across the state. They’re accountants, government analysts, nurses, IT workers, custodians and more. The union has been negotiating a new labor agreement since its contract expired on June 30, and is demanding better pay, more affordable healthcare coverage and more flexibility to work from home. CalHR, the state agency that handles state labor negotiations, said it “remains focused on achieving a fair and responsible agreement and continues to be available at the bargaining table.” With as many as 95,000 union members eligible to strike, you may experience some delays in government services.
